title: Writing down Until the Real Thing Comes Along on the riverbank
summary: Dancers Pha Terrell and Van hummed the song to him at 3 a.m. and he notated it, took no credit, and later lost the manuscript.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But, now, there was -- you know, when you set I Don't Want To Set The World On Fire, I was thinking of that other song that Fay Terro used to sing, Until The Real Thing Comes Along.
Until The Real Thing Comes Along.
Now, that's another example of a song that had to be sung at that tempo to make any sense.
That's right. And the way that got created, Fay Terro was a dancer.
Oh, was he?

And he had a dance team with a little fellow they called Van. And they got -- was getting a song together and they were dancers. And Van deceased. But they came to my house at 3:00 at night, and said, man, we got a song here, listen.

And I got up out of the bed and went down on the riverbank, and didn't have any manuscript paper. So I took some plain writing paper and made some lines and went down and sat on the riverbank and let them sing it. And I remember all the other words that they had, she had to correct. And they had lyrics in there, like I worked for you, I slaved by
fingers to the bone for you, I'll moan for you, I'll groan for you and all that. They eliminated that later.

But what happened, I wrote that out. So when I went back to Kansas City, about ten years ago, my wife's grandmother, my first wife, said, you left this thing up in the attic, that song I heard so much about. And she went up in the attic and had that original piece of paper I wrote that --
What did you do with that?
I fooled around and let it get away. She had a attic where she kept everything. She said, here's that thing, I heard that song was so big, look what you did, years ago.
Did you have your name on that?
No, I didn't write the song, they had --
Oh, I see, yeah.
I just wrote the music down for them on some writing paper, and that was still there for about 20 years up in the attic. And I said, I let that get away, that's history, and I couldn't find it.
So Fay Terro was singing in Andy's band.
Andy Capp, yeah.
So that's how it got in there.
Yeah.
I guess maybe Andy helped him out with it after he got there with the arrangements, or somebody
made arrangements on it.
Well, that was a pretty darn big hit for that time, wasn't it?
Yeah. A lot of things that come out, you don't know till you -- because that's --
Yeah. But, of course, they could sort of -- they couldn't play anything. They could cook it up in their heads --

That's all, they couldn't write the music or nothing. They hummed it to me and I wrote it down, right out there. But I had my old guitar with me, too, and we sat on the riverbank at 4:00 in the morning, that's how I wrote that down. Fay Terro and Van. And I gave him that lead sheet and he tore out with it. I don't know, maybe Mary Lou Williams might have made the arrangement on it. I don't know who made the arrangement. Andy would know, I guess.
Yeah, it was -- whatever it was, it was a very simple arrangement.
Yeah, but, see, I'm a guy never claimed nothing I didn't do. A lot of guys --
No, but it's just like --
Yeah, but they wanted me to go on the song with them.
You give away 50 percent -
Yeah, I could have went on the song
with them, but I didn't see why I should go on a song just for writing some notes down for some guys. But that's the racket today. But to me, that was dishonest, in those days.
Yeah, that was living up to your principles at that time. You wouldn't do that today, would you?

No, I wouldn't do that today. If I write anything today, more than likely I'll have to go on it because you're a part of it. You change the music around -- you know, I had to change a lot of the music, too.
Well, I was going to say, I'm sure that you don't know how many notes you put in there for it.
No, you don't. It was the only thing it was. It was pretty close to that melody, but they had enough there for three songs. Lyrics and things, I don't know.
